preexisting_partial_rows: uncounted: no reachable database. Production is Cloud SQL instance empressa-trading-prod:us-east4:cockpit-pg, database `cockpit`, user `cockpit_api`, reachable only via the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy running on the deploy-sensitive production VM. `gcloud sql instances list` confirms the instance is RUNNABLE and visible to the active account, but `gcloud secrets list --project=empressa-trading-prod` returns only `cockpit-pii-master-key` - no database credential exists in Secret Manager; the password lives in the VM's .env, so obtaining it would require SSHing the production VM, which is far beyond a read-only count. No local Postgres server, no Docker daemon, and no local *.db file exists in the tree. TO COUNT, one of these must become true: (a) the cockpit_api password or an IAM database credential is supplied so a local cloud-sql-proxy can connect read-only, or (b) someone with VM access runs: SELECT count(*) FROM atom_outcomes WHERE label='partial' AND decline_basis IS NULL; alongside SELECT label, decline_basis, count(*) FROM atom_outcomes GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2; NOTE: whatever that number is, the pre-existing portion of it can never be split - see distinction_boundary.
distinction_boundary: 0059_outcome_decline_basis (authored 2026-08-20). Rows carry the distinction only from the moment the migration is APPLIED to a given database, which is NOT the authoring date and NOT the merge date - merged is not applied, and this PR does not apply it. `alembic_version` stores no timestamp, so the applied-at instant must be recorded per environment. A future query must use `decline_basis IS NOT NULL` as the positive test for a row that carries the distinction, NEVER created_at against the authoring date, because a database migrated later will have written ambiguous rows after it. Every atom_outcomes row with label='partial' AND decline_basis IS NULL written before application is permanently ambiguous: this is the fifth derivation state, discarded at the moment of writing. The distinguishing fact existed in the grader's control flow and the write destroyed it, so no backfill was attempted and none is possible - a guessed basis would be indistinguishable from a measured one once written.
handoff_to_stopgrade: CORRECTED FROM null. It should never have been null, and the reasoning that produced it was wrong in a specific way: I wrote that 'widening the signature to Optional is a widening and cannot break that caller'. I checked the TYPE direction and never checked the CONTROL FLOW direction. Optional-ing a parameter is a widening; converting a return into a raise is not. stop_grade.py had no enclosing try at that call and its docstring says 'Never raises', so UnmeasurableRError propagated out of a function contractually forbidden to emit one. I had even recorded the 'no enclosing try' fact in swallow_audit and read it as reassuring (a refusal would 'propagate loudly') when it was the hazard. Separately I reasoned only about the branch being UNREACHABLE under the code as I read it, and #357 then deliberately MADE it reachable - so my conclusion was tied to a caller detail another lane was actively changing. WHAT IT SHOULD HAVE SAID: 'r_multiple_from_pnl now raises instead of returning 0.0. stop_grade.py:356 calls it with no enclosing try inside a function documented Never raises. If your row makes the qty branch reachable, that raise escapes. Consume r_multiple_or_decline and delete the duplicate UnknownQuantity check.' That collapse is what commit 069d9f57 performs, and it is what the comment at stop_grade.py:478 asked for by name.

Four violations rejected: declined with no basis, declined carrying a score, unknown basis value, basis on a non-declined row. constraint_verified_by_violation.sqlite: Four equivalent raw-ORM violations rejected with IntegrityError in tests/test_outcome_abstention.py, plus a test asserting both constraint names appear in the sqlite_master DDL - so the control is not vacuous in the environment CI actually runs.
constraint_verified_by_violation.why_check_not_native_enum: There is no native enum anywhere: `label` is a bare String(16). Using CHECK rather than a PostgreSQL ENUM type makes both engines enforce the identical guarantee, removing the divergence rather than assuming it away. A native PG enum would have been enforced in production and absent from SQLite tests - a control that passes review and cannot fail where it is exercised.

migration_tested_both_directions: Yes, against real PostgreSQL 18.3. Full chain `alembic upgrade head` from empty to 0059 (exit 0), then `downgrade -1` to 0058 with a declined row present - the downgrade must delete declined rows before restoring score NOT NULL, and did (exit 0; column dropped, constraints dropped, score NOT NULL restored, alembic_version back to 0058), then `upgrade head` again (exit 0, both constraints back). Local runs required a WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy wrapper; psycopg async is incompatible with the Windows ProactorEventLoop. CI is ubuntu and unaffected.

swallow_audit.question: does any caller of r_multiple_or_decline / r_multiple_from_pnl wrap it in a bare except Exception that would swallow the new refusal and re-fabricate a value one level up
swallow_audit.method: ast; for every Call to the R functions and to record_trade_outcome, walked the ancestor chain for enclosing Try nodes and reported each handler's type, body and whether it re-raises
swallow_audit.result: NO starved refusal. runner.py:1293 IS a bare except Exception with a log-only body and no re-raise, and it wraps BOTH the r_multiple_or_decline call and the record_trade_outcome call - which is exactly why the fix DEPOSITS a declined row rather than raising. A raise inside that block would be swallowed and the row dropped, which reads as 'the grader never ran', a different fact again. stop_grade.py:356 (r_multiple_from_pnl) has NO enclosing try, so a refusal there would propagate loudly; it is unreachable there anyway. outcomes.py:229 is the internal delegation, no try. routers/bots.py calls neither R function directly.
swallow_audit.residual_declared: If the declined DEPOSIT itself fails inside runner.py:1293, the row is lost. That is pre-existing best-effort behaviour (one bot must not kill the tick) and it is a DECLARED degradation, not a silent one: logger.warning with exc_info=True. Not changed here; changing exception policy in the bot tick loop is a separate concern. The end-to-end tests assert the row EXISTS precisely so this swallow cannot hide a failure from them.

deploy_gate_finding.what: The full local suite after the second pass showed 1 failure: test_deploy_gate.py::test_declared_evidence_is_not_older_than_the_control_it_describes[atom-mutation-refusal]. NOT a flake and NOT pre-existing.
deploy_gate_finding.mechanism: The control declares path app/spine/store.py, which commit 8ea3bd88 modified. Its evidence was dated 2026-08-19; git last-touch became 2026-08-20. gate.evidence_state returned 'stale' with detail 'evidence 2026-08-19, but the control changed 2026-08-20'.
deploy_gate_finding.second_mechanism_rejected: A time-based decay crossing a threshold. Rejected: evidence_state compares the declared date against git's last-touch of the path (the detail names the file's change date, not an age), and the same test passed in the FIRST local full run when the identical edits were uncommitted - uncommitted edits do not move git's last-touch, which a clock-based decay would not explain.
deploy_gate_finding.resolution: Evidence RE-GATHERED BY VIOLATION before the date was touched: stored an atom, edited claim_value_json in place, committed, confirmed AtomMutationError raised; tests/test_atom_immutability.py 11 passed. Only then was evidence_date advanced to 2026-08-20 and the evidence text amended to say it was re-gathered and how. Bumping the date without re-gathering would have been asserting evidence not collected.
deploy_gate_finding.collateral_finding: This staleness check CANNOT FIRE IN CI. CI uses a shallow checkout, where evidence_state returns 'unverifiable', which the test explicitly accepts (documented in its own docstring). It can only ever fail on a full clone. PR #361's first CI run was green WITH stale evidence for this reason. Reported, not fixed - it is the deploy-gate lane's call.
deploy_gate_finding.next_commit_checked: Intersected all control paths against the pending change set before committing the second pass: NONE matched, so no further control was staled.

reconciliation_third_pass.why_it_broke: #357 removed the qty coercion so an absent quantity reaches the shared refusal, and pinned that with a LINE-TRACE test locating the `qty <= 0` guard by ast and asserting its BODY executes. My change deleted that early-return shape and made the function raise instead.
reconciliation_third_pass.what_changed_in_stop_grade: It now CONSUMES the discriminated result instead of calling the raising variant and separately re-deriving UnknownQuantity. The duplicate check is deleted: one refusal, decided in one place, reason travelling on the result. The event still stays PENDING via _refuse returning False, which is unchanged behaviour.
reconciliation_third_pass.qty_none_not_zero: It passes qty=None rather than 0.0. The 0.0 existed only to TRIP the `qty <= 0` disjunct because the old signature could not express a refusal. Keeping it would have left a second fabrication: cf_pnl is move x pv x qty, so a 0.0 size manufactures a 0.0 counterfactual PnL - a fabricated numerator handed to the function whose job is refusing fabricated inputs.
reconciliation_third_pass.guard_precedence: r_multiple_or_decline now checks the DENOMINATOR before the NUMERATOR. Load bearing when both are absent: a caller that cannot resolve a size also cannot compute that position's PnL and must pass None for both, so attributing to the numerator would name the symptom and send an operator to exit pricing when the entry claim is what is broken. Pinned by test_denominator_is_attributed_before_numerator_when_both_are_absent.
reconciliation_third_pass.pinning_test_updated_not_weakened: tests/test_intervention_stop_grade_refusals.py keeps its line-trace character: it still locates a guard structurally by ast and asserts the guard BODY executes. It now targets r_multiple_or_decline and the `qty is None` refusal that actually fires, asserts BOTH qty guards exist so neither can be quietly deleted, and additionally asserts the NUMERATOR arrived absent - a check the old version could not make. A new test pins that the `qty <= 0` guard is still live for its own caller (bots/runner.py, whose st.qty_total domain is {None} u [0, inf)).
reconciliation_third_pass.cancellation_reverified: The stop-grade lane's algebraic result (pv and qty cancel, so counterfactual_r = move / |entry_px - stop_px|) was re-verified INDEPENDENTLY through the new code path rather than taken on trust: 200,000 randomised (entry, stop, pv, qty, cf) combinations, 0 mismatches. A known quantity still yields the correct R, so consuming a post-fix 0.0 is not reintroduced.
reconciliation_third_pass.schema_moved: No. models.py, spine/types.py and the migration are untouched in this pass, so the migration was not re-run; it was already verified up and down against PostgreSQL 18.3 in the second pass.
